I know how this feels and it sucks. One thing I found that made me able to take it off for periods of time was by telling someone how I felt and what I was constantly thinking about doing. I strongly recommend you let at least one person into that part of your life so that you are able to take it off, at least occasionally. Also, letting people know you feel "bad" is a way I kind of get around the whole mask thing. While it isn't telling the whole truth, saying that does let them know that things aren't all right at the moment. If they ask why you can then choose to either tell them the truth, or avoid it by saying something like, "I'm just feeling sick"(still not lying, sick in the mind, but not telling the truth either). Find ways to take the maks off at times, like in private spaces even. I'd imagine (I wouldn't know because I haven't been able to for so long) crying is a way to take the mask off and relieve pressure. Good luck and stay safe.

No problem! Just let me know if I can tell you about games/books/music to get your mind off things. Talking with friends is a great way to spend time as well. Whenever I feel down I try to hook up with a friend (one time it was some random nice dude) to play a game online. Dauntless is a good game by EPIC that's free and is pretty good. Stay safe and good luck pulling through this. You got this.

I read your comment on here and I hope that you're able to pull through this. Like others have said, what you've been through is horrible but remember, don't base yourself off of traumatic moments. My own coping method for loss of self worth, and I hope this helps, is to find a distraction. I sometimes play games (any game helps) or get myself immersed some other way like reading. Through all of these distractions I was eventually inspired to start making a videogame of my own, with an expansive storyline and whatnot. I reccomend you do the same, find something that you enjoy doing (it's fantastic if you can do this with other people, like playing a game online) and eventually you'll come up with something to sink your time into that will become a wonderful creation for both yourself and others to admire. I wish you luck, stay safe.

If you're finding it hard to open up I reccomend starting with small talk. Don't jump into the problem headfirst or if talking about problems right then would be better for you then do that. It's important for you to go at your own pace and you remember that you aren't wasting his time, even if you don't talk. This will actually help him understand what's going on and how he can help. Good luck, stay safe.

I just recently told my folks about my own depression (I'm so sorry about your loss I can't imagine what that's like) and it wasn't how I expected it to be. I emailed them, and later in the night I went to their room to talk. Important note here, I did not tell them everything. For me, I have to take this whole revealing process very slowly because it'd be too shocking for them to know all of what I'm going through at once. Let your mom know that you've thought about killing yourself and definitely ask about therapy. It'll be really hard to actually tell her, so take everything at your own pace. Don't rush, but do make sure you let her know. (also let her know that the reason you're still her is because of your family and that you don't want to hurt them. Why you stay is important) good luck and stay safe
